item.title: Ideal balanced pairs in n-exangulated categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.28657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is devoted to ideal approximation theory in $n$-exangulated categories. We define ideal balanced pairs and explore their properties and equivalent characterizations. We prove that any complete ideal cotorsion triple $(\mathcal{I},\mathcal{K},\mathcal{J})$ satisfying suitable assumptions yields an ideal balanced pair $(\mathcal{I}, \mathcal{J})$, and the converse holds under additional hypotheses. We further show that for an ideal balanced pair, it is equivalent to an additive subfunctor with enough projective morphisms and enough injective morphisms.
item.dc:creator: Peiyu Zhang, Zhuolin Zheng, Li Wang, Dajun Liu

item.title: Logic vs doctrines, a mirror symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2610.29771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies doctrines in categorical logic and their relations to fragments of geometric logic. After a brief account of the historical context for the notion of doctrine in categorical logic, we propose our working definition. We then show that there is a Galois connection between the poset of doctrines and the poset of fragments of geometric logic as defined in the framework of Kan injectivity in the 2-category of topoi, recently developed by the first and third authors. Concretely, the connection is realised by a general construction of syntactic categories and classifying topoi which encompasses all well-known examples in categorical logic. This yields a mirror symmetry, between the algebraic world of doctrines and the geometric world of topoi: to provide evidence of this phenomenon, we prove a few symmetric results relating doctrines and logics by means of syntactic categories and classifying topoi. We conclude with a discussion on the theme of conceptual completeness.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Di Liberti, Umberto Tarantino, Lingyuan Ye

item.title: Day Convolution and Homotopy Groups on the Pointed Homotopy Category of CW Complexes
item.description: arXiv:2610.29239v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We freely enrich the pointed homotopy category of CW complexes over abelian groups and equip the resulting functor category with the enriched Day convolution induced by the smash product. After identifying the convolution unit and recording the coherence maps, we compute the convolution of the homotopy-group functors. For integers $n,m\geq 2$ we construct a natural isomorphism $\pi_n\star\pi_m\cong\pi_{n+m}$ induced by the external smash product; equivalently, the external smash product is the universal natural pairing of homotopy groups. Under this identification, the symmetry interchanging the two factors acts on $\pi_{n+m}$ by multiplication by $(-1)^{nm}$.
item.dc:creator: Abhiram Srinivas Yedathore

item.title: Curvature, second variation and Jacobi fields in elastic diffeology
item.description: arXiv:2610.29360v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop curvature theory on Blohmann's elastic diffeological spaces. We introduce curvature-tensorial connections, whose curvature factors uniquely through $T_3M$, and show that this property holds on finite-dimensional manifolds and is preserved on mapping spaces. Using a plotwise commutator identity and the elasticity axioms, we establish the classical curvature symmetries for curvature-tensorial Levi-Civita connections. We define sectional curvature and a curvature form on the algebraic exterior square, and demonstrate an obstruction to the usual Ricci trace construction: on $C^\infty(S^1,S^2)$, the relevant curvature endomorphism extends boundedly to the $L^2$ completion but is not trace class. We prove the second variation formula, identify the energy Hessian with the index form, and characterize its null space. Under additional hypotheses, we establish existence and uniqueness of Jacobi fields with prescribed initial data. Finally, non-positive sectional curvature excludes conjugate points, while a negative index direction obstructs length minimization.
item.dc:creator: Yusuke Shiobara

item.title: Coherent differentiation with a monoid of degrees: derivatives, Taylor expansion, finite differences...
item.description: arXiv:2610.29874v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coherent differentiation has been introduced a few years ago as a refinement of the (categorical semantics of the) differential lambda-calculus and of differential linear logic, compatible with the determinism of computation, and hence in categories where addition of morphisms in the hom-sets is only partially defined. In this setting differentiation is implemented by a kind of ''tangent functor'', with the difference that it maps an object to its object of summable tuples rather to a tangent bundle. In our earlier work, these tuples were pairs in the case of simple differentiation, and families indexed by integers when dealing with Taylor expansion and the Fa{\`a} di Bruno formula. We push this idea further, considering now tuples indexed by an arbitrary commutative partial monoid satisfying a nonnegativity condition. The monoid structure on these indices plays a crucial role in the definition of the ''differential'' calculus associated with this ''tangent functor''. In that way, and without changing the general categorical infrastructure of coherent differentiation, this theory accommodates new notions of ''differentiation'' of which we describe several instances. Among many others, such notions include various forms of finite differences as well as Taylor expansion truncated at any fixed degree, and finite Taylor expansion of a fixed finite degree with a remainder.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Ehrhard (IRIF), Aymeric Walch

item.title: Lax descent and foliated Verdier duality
item.description: arXiv:2610.29977v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Higher categorical methods allow us to view recollements as lax descent data and build a corresponding descent theory governed by an $\infty$-bicategorical theory of limits. We demonstrate some concrete innovations brought along by these new techniques in the classical context of constructible and perverse sheaves on stratified spaces. Our first application uses partially (op)lax descent to recover the famous result of Beilinson telling us how to glue perverse sheaves in terms of vanishing and nearby cycles. The remainder of the article is concerened with establishing a uniform view on a series of classification results for perverse sheaves culminating in recent work of Kapranov-Schechtman. Namely, we use lax descent to establish a ``foliated'' variant of Verdier duality which, informally speaking, identifies the derived constructible category of a suitably foliated space with sections of a categorical cosheaf on the leaf space whose stalks are the categories of sheaves along the leaves. Again, this is obtained as an application of lax descent, and seems to provide a reasonable framework to formalize the idea of ``mixed sheaf-cosheaf objects'' promoted by Kapranov and Schechtman.
item.dc:creator: Tobias Dyckerhoff, Till Heine, Simon Schneider, Kostiantyn Tolmachov

item.title: Partial actions of groups on monoidal categories
item.description: arXiv:2412.13123v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we introduce the notion of a partial action of a group on a strict monoidal category. We propose, in the context of Monoidal categories, new constructions analogous to those existing for partial group actions over an algebra such as the globalization, the subalgebra of partial invariants, and the partial smash product.
item.dc:creator: Eliezer Batista, Felipe Lopes Castro, Mykola Khrypchenko

item.title: A nontopological triangulated category which is $\theta$-dg enhanced
item.description: arXiv:2610.25198v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every nonzero commutative ring $R$ and infinite cardinal $\theta$, we construct a nontopological triangulated category over $R$, whose thick subcategories generated by $<\theta$ objects admit $R$-linear dg enhancements, while the scalar action of $R$ is faithful.
item.dc:creator: Chencheng Zhang

item.title: Simple-shifted monoidal derived equivalences for tensor categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.26196v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate monoidal derived equivalences between tensor categories with infinitely many isomorphism classes of simple objects. We introduce the notion of a simple-shifted monoidal derived equivalence and prove that a simple-shifted monoidal derived equivalence gives rise to a tensor equivalence. In addition, we investigate which tensor categories have the property that every monoidal derived equivalence between them is necessarily simple-shifted, and we establish some sufficient conditions for this property. As a corollary, we show that a monoidal derived equivalence between pointed tensor categories implies a tensor equivalence between them.
item.dc:creator: Jing Yu

item.title: Central series of cocommutative Hopf braces
item.description: arXiv:2605.03798v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: By extending some classical results known for groups and skew braces, we define and investigate central series of cocommutative Hopf braces. Both left and right central series are defined using a $\star$-product that measures the difference between the two algebra operations, and naturally leads to introducing the notions of socle and of annihilator of a cocommutative Hopf brace. We characterize the central extensions relative to the subcategories of cocommutative Hopf algebras and of commutative and cocommutative Hopf algebras, respectively. Since the category of cocommutative Hopf braces is semi-abelian and it has enough projectives with respect to the class of cleft extensions, one can then establish suitable Hopf formulae for their homology. These are expressed in terms of the corresponding notions of relative commutators of cocommutative Hopf braces. In particular, the one relative to the subcategory of commutative and cocommutative Hopf algebras turns out to be the Huq commutator.
item.dc:creator: Maria Bevilacqua, Marino Gran, Andrea Sciandra

item.title: DisCo Algebra: Why Disintegration and Combination Are Not Inverses
item.description: arXiv:2610.15006v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present DisCo algebra---a compositional framework for joint probability built from a symmetric cooperad (disintegration) and a magma-operad (non-associative partial combination, restricted to the image of disintegration) on the bare family $\mathcal{P}_n=\mathrm{Prob}([0,1]^n)$. No probability integral transform, no external summary functions, no enrichment of objects with conditional kernels. The disintegration side uses block-wise joint CDFs as intrinsic, measure-determined 1D summaries, yielding a lossy compression. The combination side reads the same summaries and reconstructs via regular conditional measures, yielding a lossless embedding on admissible inputs. We prove that combination followed by disintegration is the identity on admissible inputs, but disintegration followed by combination is not---it defines a renormalization operator $R_{\mathcal{I}}=\text{Combine}\circ\text{Disintegrate}$. The information loss of this operator is exactly the probability curvature $\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{I}}(\mu)$---the conditional KL divergence between the true conditional distribution and the conditionally independent product. This curvature measures the obstruction to lossless decomposition and reveals a hard limit on how much cross-block dependence can be captured by CDF-based scalar block summaries.
item.dc:creator: Xuexing Lu

item.title: Approximability of Triangulated Categories under Separable Extensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.27031v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the behavior of approximability under separable extensions of triangulated categories. Let $\mathcal{B}$ be an approximable triangulated category and let $\mathbf{T}=(T,\theta,\mu)$ be a smashing, stably separable exact monad on $\mathcal{B}$. Assume that the category of $\mathbf{T}$-modules $\mathbf{T}\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathcal{B}}$ admits a canonical triangulated structure. We prove that if $T$ is right $t$-exact with respect to a $t$-structure in the preferred equivalence class of $\mathcal{B}$, then $\mathbf{T}\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathcal{B}}$ is again an approximable triangulated category. As an application, we show that, under suitable assumptions, a smashing localization functor on an approximable triangulated category induces a recollement of approximable triangulated categories, thereby yielding a converse-type result to the gluing theorem of Burke--Neeman--Pauwels. Finally, under suitable hypotheses, we prove that separable extensions restrict naturally to the intrinsic subcategories associated with approximable triangulated categories.
item.dc:creator: Mengzhen Zhu, Yuefei Zheng, Xianhui Fu
